title: Compartmentation of trace metals in Cymodocea nodosa from a heavily polluted area (Central Gulf of Gabes; Southern Mediterranean Sea): Potential use of the seagrass as environmental monitoring and bioremediation tool
summary: Seabed sediments were the main source of metals taken up by this seagrass. It stores some metals in roots and moves others to leaves. The authors suggest it could serve as a pollution indicator and a clean-up tool.

findings.headline: Sediments are the main source of metals taken up by seagrass
findings.summary: Seabed sediments were the main source of contaminants bioaccumulated in Cymodocea nodosa.
